text:
The derivation starts from the pure‑state wavefunction  
\[
\psi = \sqrt{\mathcal P}\,e^{iS/\hbar},
\]  
so that the Madelung–Bohm velocities are  
\[
\pi_\mu = \frac{1}{m}\,\partial_\mu S ,\qquad 
u_\mu = \frac{\hbar}{2}\,\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal P .
\]

Writing the parameter derivative of the state,
\[
\partial_\mu\psi = \psi\Bigl[\frac{1}{2}\partial_\mu\ln\mathcal P
        + i\,\frac{m}{\hbar}\,\pi_\mu\Bigr]
      = \frac{\psi}{\hbar}\bigl(u_\mu+i\,m\pi_\mu\bigr),
\]
and inserting this into the definition of the quantum Fisher (Fubini–Study) metric,
\[
g^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mu\nu}=4\,
\bigl[\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle
      -\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle\bigr],
\]
one finds that the imaginary cross‑terms cancel and the remaining real part is
\[
g^{\mathrm{FS}}_{\mu\nu}= \frac{4m^{2}}{\hbar^{2}}
\Bigl[\operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu,\pi_\nu)
      +\operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu,u_\nu)\Bigr]_{\mathcal P}.
\]

Hence the proportionality factor \(C\) multiplying the covariances is

\[
C = \frac{4\,m^{2}}{\hbar^{2}}.
\]

Using the placeholder \(x = \hbar\) to avoid the symbol \(\hbar\),

\[
\boxed{C = \dfrac{4\,m^{2}}{x^{2}} }.
\]

ANSWER: 4*m^2/x^2
